about: Shared contract for the vaults snapshot (the memory graph: each Obsidian vault the owner names in vaults.yml, as dots and lines). The same bytes live in agent-team-template and agent-cockpit; a test in each repo checks they match. The collector writes `sample`-shaped files; the board reads them. A vault is published at one of two levels. `shape` is the default: the vault name, counts, and anonymous dots (numbers) joined by lines (number pairs) - no title, folder, tag, date, content or path. `titles` is the owner's opt-in, per vault: it adds each note's title, its top folder, its day, and a hub dot for each day or tag that two or more notes share - every one of them held to the title rule below. A note's contents are read in memory to find its links and are never kept at either level. The vault's location on the computer is never kept.

titleRule.note: A title is whatever a note is called, so it is held to what the board will show: not empty, no space at either end, 80 characters at most, none of the never fragments (compared without regard to case: an at sign, either slash, the start of a signed token or a key, an authorization header), no control or invisible character, no stretch of 24 or more characters between separators, no id, and - on the collector only, because only it knows them - not the owner's username, computer name or home folder. A title that fails is not published; its note is an anonymous dot and is counted. The same rule holds a top folder name, a tag value and a hub label.

names.note: A vault is called by its folder name, held to the connection-name rule in connections-parity.json (a name the board would refuse is not published; the vault is counted as hidden).

rules: a block (vaults) with any status other than found carries only status and an optional why; why is one of whyCodes - never a message and never a word of what was refused. `not found` is the ordinary answer: no vault is named in vaults.yml, or none of those named is on this computer

only vaults named in vaults.yml are ever opened, up to caps.vaults; a vault the owner did not name is never read, and its name is not kept. A vault is found by its folder name in Obsidian's own list of vaults; where it lives on the computer is read in memory to open it and is never kept
level is `shape` unless vaults.yml says exactly `titles` for that vault. At `shape` a vault has no nodes, no hubs and no untitled: only counts, and edges between numbered dots

a dot is a note, numbered from 0 in the order of the notes' paths in the vault (sorted without regard to case, then by the path itself); notes is how many dots, at most caps.notes. Notes past the cap are counted in more, and notes withheld - bigger than noteMaxBytes, a link, or unreadable - in hidden

an edge is [from, to, kind] with kind an index into edgeKinds: 0 link, 1 mention, 2 day, 3 tag. A line has no direction: from is below to. link is a wikilink or an embed of a note ([[Note]], [[folder/Note#heading|alias]], ![[Note]]) resolved the way Obsidian does: a path-qualified link matches that path from the vault root, or ends with it; otherwise the note's name matches without regard to case; when more than one note matches, the one with the shortest path wins, then the first path in order. mention is a markdown link to a note ([text](folder/note.md)), relative to the note it is written in. A link that resolves to no note, to the note itself, to a file that is not a note, or outside the vault, is not a line. Links inside code are not links. One line per pair and kind

at the titles level only, a hub dot stands for a day or a tag that at least minHubNotes notes share. Hubs are numbered from notes, after the dots, in the order of their kind (days first) and label. A note joins a day hub by [note, hub, 2] and a tag hub by [note, hub, 3]; a hub never joins two hubs or two notes, so thirty notes on one day are thirty lines, not four hundred and thirty-five. A note's day is a date at the start of its file name (2026-10-09 Plan.md) or, failing that, its frontmatter date or created. Its tags are its frontmatter tags, tag, project and people values, up to maxTagsPerNote

lines is how many edges. lonely is how many notes have no link or mention line: a note nothing links to and that links to nothing. Over caps.lines, the hub lines go first (tags, then days), then the mentions, then the links; every line left out is counted in moreLines, and a hub left with fewer than minHubNotes lines is left out with them

a vault's part of the file is at most vaultBytesBudget bytes, so three vaults fit the file limit with room to spare. A vault over it loses its hubs and their lines first, then its last notes, ten per hundred at a time, and every note and line it loses is counted in more and moreLines

at the titles level, nodes has one entry per dot, in order: title, folder and day are each there only when the note has one and it passes the title rule (a day is a real calendar day). A note whose title fails the rule is an anonymous dot with no title, and untitled counts them. The folder is the note's top folder; a note at the root has none

a note's contents are read in memory to find its links, its day and its tags, and are never kept: nothing a note says, no heading, no excerpt, no path. A vault, a note, a folder or a title the collector could not read or refuse is counted, never described

the file is written when what it says has changed, or at least rewriteAfterHours after the last write, so a vault that does not change adds one small file a day to the team repo, not one every three hours; a computer with no vault named and no earlier file writes nothing
a file older than staleAfterDays is shown as not updated since its time, never as the current graph
the board shows at most maxComputersShown computers, newest takenAt first

resolution.note: Each case is a vault (its note paths, from the vault root), one note in it and that note's text, and the lines that note makes: the note each link reaches and the kind (link for a wikilink or an embed, mention for a markdown link), links first, then in path order. A vault's lines are all of its notes' cases at once. The collector builds the graph this way for an extra vault; the board builds the same lines for the team repo, so both hold to this table.

cases.why: a plain wikilink finds the note by its name, wherever it is
an alias is not part of the name
a heading or a block reference is not part of the name, and one note is one line
an embed of a note is a link
an embed of a file that is not a note is nothing
case does not matter
the extension may be written
spaces round the name are not part of it
a path from the vault root is exact
a path that is only the end of a longer path still matches
a path with folders in it never reaches a note that merely has the same name
two notes with one name: the one with the fewest folders wins
the fewest folders wins, even when a path with more folders is shorter
a note at the root beats the same name in a folder
the same number of folders: the shorter path wins, then the first in order
a link to a note that is not there is nothing
a link to a folder is nothing
a note linking to itself, or to a heading in itself, is nothing
code is not text: a link inside a fence or between backticks is not a link
one line for a pair and a kind, however often it is linked
a markdown link to a note is a mention, from the folder of the note it is written in
two dots climb a folder
one dot is this folder
a leading slash is the vault root
a space is written %20 or inside angle brackets, and both mean the same note
a fragment, a query or a title is not part of the path
an address is not a note
a markdown link to a file that is not a note, or that climbs out of the vault, is nothing
a markdown link needs the .md, as Obsidian writes it
case does not matter in a markdown path either
a wikilink and a markdown link to the same note are two lines, a link and a mention
a link in the frontmatter counts
several links make several lines, in path order
